characters.summary: Etrigan the Demon is a rhyming demon bound to the human Jason Blood, with mystically enhanced strength, a powerful healing factor, hellfire projection and a high command of magic.

techniques: Hellfire projection, usually from his mouth

mechanisms: Healing factor that can handle an incredible amount of damage

weaknesses: Holy powers, holy water and iron
Helpless against those with magic strong enough to control him, such as Morgaine le Fey
limitations: Bound to Jason Blood; the change is triggered by reciting the poem from Merlin's crypt

sources.supports: Powers: mystically enhanced strength, healing factor, hellfire/flame breath, energy blasts, high command of magic, super speed and agility; weakness to holy powers, holy water and iron, and to those with magic strong enough to control him (Morgaine le Fey); bond to Jason Blood via Merlin's poem; defeated by Donna Troy's Lasso of Persuasion.

notableResults.citation: Wikipedia: Etrigan the Demon (no issue named)
notableResults.note: Defeated when Donna Troy used her Lasso of Persuasion.

campaignTags.claim: Has a very high command of magic.
Projects hellfire from his body, usually from his mouth.
Healing factor can handle an incredible amount of damage.

unknowns: Exact limits of hellfire resistance vary across different creative runs.

Removed by review (not supported by the cited source): defense: Superhuman durability; defense: Demonic regeneration; defense: Mystic resilience; limitation: Transformation depends on the rhyming invocation spoken by or for Jason Blood; feat: Fought evenly against major magical and physical threats in the DC Universe using hellfire and brute strength.; result: Superman; tag: Possesses inherent demonic magic and casts rhyming spells.

Corrected 2026-11-13 (Claude second pass): restored healing factor and strength (the page does support them); removed "demon sword strikes" and flight/leaping (not on the page; the sword skill is Jason Blood's). Rhyming is a result of a promotion in Hell, not a spell mechanism. Added fire-control and self-regeneration tags.

characters.continuity: DC Comics Post-Crisis (Ronnie Raymond, fused with Martin Stein or Jason Rusch)
characters.summary: Firestorm is Ronnie Raymond fused with Martin Stein or Jason Rusch through the Firestorm matrix, with elemental transmutation, energy projection and absorption, flight and intangibility.
limitations: Depends on the fusion: Stein supplies guidance from inside his mind; without it he lacked the knowledge to use his powers wisely (Extreme Justice era)

sources.supports: Firestorm (character) article: elemental transmutation, energy projection and absorption, flight, intangibility; fusion with Stein or Rusch, Stein as the voice of reason in his mind; Ronnie later taken over by the Firestorm matrix.

campaignTags.claim: Flight is among his listed powers, from the Firestorm matrix itself.

unknowns: Exact upper limits of mass transmutation without fatigue.

Removed by review (not supported by the cited source): technique: Energy projection; defense: Energy shields; weakness: Mental coordination required between fused minds; limitation: Requires active cooperation of both minds in the matrix to operate at full capacity; feat: Transmuted a mountain of concrete into harmless snow.

Corrected 2026-11-13 (Claude second pass): removed the result "Justice League members: win" (the page mentions confrontations with the League but no outcome) and the "regenerative atomic reconstruction" defense and "matrix disruption" weakness (not on the page). Source URL updated to the article it redirects to.

characters.continuity: DC Comics mainstream, post-Infinite Crisis Dru-Zod (general Kryptonian traits per Wikipedia)
characters.summary: General Zod is a Kryptonian military leader with all the standard powers of a Kryptonian under a yellow sun. He fights with ruthless tactical precision and advanced combat training.

mechanisms: Virtual invulnerability and accelerated healing under a yellow sun

limitations: His powers are often inferior to Superman's

sources.supports: Kryptonian physiology under yellow sun, military background, and powers.

notableResults.citation: Superman: War of the Supermen, per Wikipedia
notableResults.note: Pushed back into the Phantom Zone by his son, Chris Kent.

campaignTags.claim: Flies using Kryptonian physiology under a yellow sun.

unknowns: Vulnerability to magic remains consistent with standard Kryptonian baselines.

Removed by review (not supported by the cited source): technique: Super-strength punches; technique: Supersonic speed blitz; defense: Super-dense cellular structure; limitation: Powers completely depend on yellow sun radiation and oxygen; result: Superman

Corrected 2026-11-13 (Claude second pass): removed "fought Superman to a standstill" (the page says nothing of the kind and says his powers are often inferior to Superman's). Other Zods on the page (pocket universe, Russian, film) are different continuities and are not used here.

characters.summary: Giganta (Doris Zeul) can grow from roughly 6'6" to several hundred feet in seconds; at giant size she is one of the strongest women in the DC Universe.

mechanisms: Skin tough enough that vampire fangs cannot pierce it
Increased durability and mass while giant

weaknesses: Not established by the cited source

sources.supports: Size from roughly 6'6" to several hundred feet; one of the strongest women at giant size; inescapable grip; vampire fangs cannot pierce her skin; losses to Wonder Woman, Hercules and Pandora.

notableResults.note: Wonder Woman quickly knocked her out.

campaignTags.claim: Can grow from roughly 6'6" to several hundred feet in seconds.
Documented at several hundred feet at full size.

unknowns: Exact maximum height limit in modern continuity revisions.

Removed by review (not supported by the cited source): technique: Giant-scale punches; technique: Throwing heavy objects; defense: Regenerative recovery from minor trauma; weakness: Vulnerable to mental attacks and specialized anti-metahuman restraints; weakness: Large target profile; limitation: Size-change has upper boundaries and requires concentration; mobility: Standard foot travel; feat: Grew to giant size and lifted a full city bus to hurl at Wonder Woman.

Corrected 2026-11-13 (Claude second pass): the earlier "lasso" detail and leaping were unsupported; results and powers now come straight from the page. Promoted from needs-review to provisional: the flag was for missing support, which is now fixed.

characters.summary: Gorilla Grodd is a hyper-intelligent super-gorilla combining immense brute strength with devastating telepathic and telekinetic capabilities.

mechanisms: Durable enough to resist supersonic punches from the Flash

weaknesses: Captain Comet can repel his mental energy

sources.supports: Telepathy, control of others' minds, vast telekinesis including force beams, great superhuman strength, durable enough to resist supersonic punches from the Flash, enhanced speed from the Light's energies; Captain Comet can repel his mental energy; defeated by the Flash and by Batman's team.

notableResults.note: The Flash defeated him and temporarily removed his telepathy.

campaignTags.claim: Described as a hyper-intelligent telepathic gorilla.
Vast telekinetic abilities ranging from force beams.
Able to control the minds of others.

unknowns: Full extent of telepathic reach across planetary distances.

Removed by review (not supported by the cited source): technique: Mental blasts; technique: Brute force strikes; defense: Telepathic shields; weakness: Arrogance; weakness: Vulnerable to superior mental defenses; limitation: Telepathy requires line of sight or focused concentration for complex control; mobility: Acrobatic leaping; feat: Mentally dominated an entire stadium of spectators simultaneously.; result: The Flash

Corrected 2026-11-13 (Claude second pass): restored page-supported strength, durability and results; speed is conditional on the Light's energies; mind control of animals is not on the page. Promoted from needs-review to provisional.

characters.summary: Green Arrow (Oliver Queen) is described as the world's greatest archer, a competent swordsman and martial artist, with trick arrows such as glue, explosive, grappling hook, flash grenade, tear gas and kryptonite arrows.

techniques: Trick arrows: glue, explosive-tipped, grappling hook, flash grenade, tear gas, kryptonite

sources.supports: World's greatest archer; swordsman and martial artist; trick arrows (glue, explosive-tipped, grappling hook, flash grenade, tear gas, kryptonite); human. Read 2026-11-13 via Wikiwand.

campaignTags.claim: Uses trick arrows such as glue, explosive, grappling hook, flash grenade, tear gas and kryptonite arrows.

unknowns: Effectiveness of specialized arrows against heavy cosmic armor.

Removed by review (not supported by the cited source): technique: Hand-to-hand combat; technique: Precise archery; defense: Tactical dodging; defense: Defensive melee blocks; weakness: Dependent on physical ammunition supply; limitation: Limited quiver capacity requiring tactical conservation; mobility: Acrobatics; mobility: Grappling hook traversal; feat: Shot an arrow through the barrel of a fired gun from a distance.

Corrected 2026-11-13 (Claude second pass): removed the Count Vertigo win and light body armor (not on the page) and the cryogenic arrow; restored archery and martial arts. Promoted from needs-review to provisional.

characters.summary: Hal Jordan wields a Green Lantern power ring fueled by willpower, enabling him to construct hard-light objects, fly at interstellar speeds, and project intense energy beams.
limitations: Constructs are limited by his imagination and willpower

sources.supports: Power ring capabilities, willpower scaling, and construct generation.

notableResults.note: Defeated Sinestro in direct ring duel.

conditional.ability: Hard-light construct generation and energy projection
conditional.dependsOn: Green Lantern Power Ring and Lantern Battery charge

campaignTags.claim: His ring grants him flight and space travel.

unknowns: Exact limits of willpower endurance under extreme psychological torture.

Removed by review (not supported by the cited source): technique: Energy blasts; technique: Ring-generated force fields; defense: Automatic life support ring barrier; weakness: Historical vulnerability to yellow color in older continuity; limitation: Ring requires periodic recharging via power battery; feat: Constructed a giant working fighter jet complex to intercept airborne missiles.

Corrected 2026-11-13 (Claude second pass): flight comes from the ring, so the tag is powered-flight, not natural-flight. The 24-hour recharge, the yellow impurity and faster-than-light travel are not on the page.

characters.continuity: DC Comics, Hal Jordan as the Spectre (Day of Judgment, 1999, until he relinquished the role)
characters.summary: After Day of Judgment, Hal Jordan became the Spectre's host, styling himself a Spirit of Redemption to atone for Parallax, with the Spectre's near-omnipotent magical and physical abilities.

mechanisms: Spectre physiology (the page cites intangibility, not invulnerability)

weaknesses: Vulnerable to the Spear of Destiny, which can kill the Spectre
limitations: Subject to divine laws and tasks set by the Presence
Hal cast himself as a Spirit of Redemption rather than Vengeance
characters.formDifferences: Replaces the power ring with the Spectre-Force's near-omnipotent magic, bounded by the Presence's laws and the Spear of Destiny weakness.

sources.supports: Near-omnipotent magical and physical abilities, superhuman strength, flight, mental abilities; needs a human host; bound by the Presence's laws; vulnerable to the Spear of Destiny; Hal as Spirit of Redemption; Hal prevailed over Asmodel for the Spectre's powers.
Asmodel bonded to the Spectre and used its power to freeze Hell; the Spectre-Force chose Hal as host.

notableResults.citation: Day of Judgment (1999), per Wikipedia: Spectre
notableResults.note: Battled Asmodel, who had bonded to the Spectre, for its powers and prevailed.

campaignTags.claim: Has the Spectre's near-omnipotent magical abilities.

unknowns: Exact limitations imposed by divine mandate during combat.
Removed by review (not supported by the cited source): defense: Invulnerability to conventional physical and energy attacks; mobility: Omnipresent teleportation
Flagged needs-review: extreme or conceptual power scaling needs owner ruling.

Corrected 2026-11-13 (Claude second pass): sourced against the current Spectre article (the old URL redirects). The "divine protection" and "susceptible to cosmic magic" claims were unsupported and are replaced by sourced limits. The broad "magic" tag was dropped as redundant with spellcaster.
